title: A weekend by the Caspian
intro: For people in Tehran, 'going north' (شمال رفتن) means one thing: a few hours' drive over the mountains to the green, rainy provinces on the Caspian Sea. Reza, Mina and Sara set off on a Thursday morning for Gilan – rice fields, rain, the grey sea, and fried fish with kateh for dinner. Look for comparatives (سبزتر 'greener', خنک‌تر 'cooler', بزرگ‌تر از 'bigger than'), اگر with a negative subjunctive, the past continuous, and the idiom خوابش برد 'she fell asleep'.
source: An original story for this course.

sentences.fa: پنجشنبه صبح، رضا و مینا و سارا با ماشین به طرف شمال راه افتادند.
sentences.r: panjshanbe sobh, Rezā o Minā o Sārā bā māshin be taraf-e shomāl rāh oftādand.
sentences.en: On Thursday morning Reza, Mina and Sara set off by car for the north.

sentences.fa: سارا پرسید: «بابا، کی به دریا می‌رسیم؟»
sentences.r: Sārā porsid: «bābā, key be daryā mi-resim?»
sentences.en: Sara asked: "Dad, when will we get to the sea?"

sentences.fa: رضا گفت: «اگر جاده شلوغ نباشد، چهار ساعت دیگر.»
sentences.r: Rezā goft: «agar jādde sholugh na-bāshad, chahār sā'at-e digar.»
sentences.en: Reza said: "If the road isn't busy, in four hours."

sentences.fa: بعد از قزوین، کوه‌ها کم‌کم سبزتر شدند.
sentences.r: ba'd az Ghazvin, kuh-hā kam-kam sabz-tar shodand.
sentences.en: After Qazvin the mountains slowly grew greener.

sentences.fa: نزدیک رشت، همه‌جا پر از شالیزار بود.
sentences.r: nazdik-e Rasht, hame-jā por az shālizār bud.
sentences.en: Near Rasht there were rice fields everywhere.

sentences.fa: زن‌ها با چکمه در آب ایستاده بودند و برنج می‌کاشتند.
sentences.r: zan-hā bā chakme dar āb istāde budand o berenj mi-kāshtand.
sentences.en: Women in boots were standing in the water, planting rice.

sentences.fa: ناگهان باران شروع شد و مینا گفت: «در شمال همیشه باران می‌آید!»
sentences.r: nāgahān bārān shoru' shod o Minā goft: «dar shomāl hamishe bārān mi-āyad!»
sentences.en: Suddenly it started to rain, and Mina said: "It always rains in the north!"

sentences.fa: اما سارا باران را دوست داشت، چون هوا خنک‌تر و بوی خاک تازه بود.
sentences.r: ammā Sārā bārān rā dust dāsht, chon havā khonak-tar o bu-ye khāk tāze bud.
sentences.en: But Sara liked the rain, because the air was cooler and the earth smelt fresh.

sentences.fa: عصر به انزلی رسیدند و یک‌راست کنار دریا رفتند.
sentences.r: asr be Anzali residand o yek-rāst kenār-e daryā raftand.
sentences.en: In the late afternoon they reached Anzali and went straight down to the sea.

sentences.fa: دریای خزر خاکستری و بزرگ بود و موج‌ها به ساحل می‌خوردند.
sentences.r: daryā-ye Khazar khākestari o bozorg bud o mowj-hā be sāhel mi-khordand.
sentences.en: The Caspian was grey and huge, and the waves were breaking on the beach.

sentences.fa: سارا کفش‌هایش را درآورد و در آب سرد دوید.
sentences.r: Sārā kafsh-hā-yash rā dar-āvard o dar āb-e sard david.
sentences.en: Sara took off her shoes and ran into the cold water.

sentences.fa: او فریاد زد: «دریا از استخر مدرسه خیلی بزرگ‌تر است!»
sentences.r: u faryād zad: «daryā az estakhr-e madrese kheyli bozorg-tar ast!»
sentences.en: She shouted: "The sea is much bigger than the school swimming pool!"

sentences.fa: شب در یک رستوران کوچک، ماهی سفید سرخ‌کرده و کته خوردند.
sentences.r: shab dar yek resturān-e kuchak, māhi-ye sefid-e sorkh-karde o kate khordand.
sentences.en: In the evening, in a little restaurant, they ate fried white fish and kateh.

sentences.fa: صاحب رستوران گفت: «کته غذای ساده‌ی گیلانی‌هاست، ولی با ماهی تازه، از هر غذایی خوشمزه‌تر است.»
sentences.r: sāheb-e resturān goft: «kate ghazā-ye sāde-ye gilāni-hā-st, vali bā māhi-ye tāze, az har ghazā-yi khoshmaze-tar ast.»
sentences.en: The owner of the restaurant said: "Kateh is the simple food of the people of Gilan, but with fresh fish it's tastier than anything."

sentences.fa: روز بعد، وقتی به تهران برمی‌گشتند، سارا در ماشین خوابش برد.
sentences.r: ruz-e ba'd, vaghti be Tehrān bar-mi-gashtand, Sārā dar māshin khāb-ash bord.
sentences.en: The next day, as they were driving back to Tehran, Sara fell asleep in the car.

sentences.fa: مینا به رضا گفت: «ماه بعد دوباره بیاییم؟»
sentences.r: Minā be Rezā goft: «māh-e ba'd dobāre biyāyim?»
sentences.en: Mina said to Reza: "Shall we come again next month?"

sentences.fa: رضا لبخند زد و گفت: «حتماً! این بار با امیر و تام.»
sentences.r: Rezā labkhand zad o goft: «hatman! in bār bā Amir o Tām.»
sentences.en: Reza smiled and said: "Definitely! And this time with Amir and Tom."

vocab.en: kateh, simple rice cooked until the water is absorbed

questions.q: How long would the drive take if the road wasn't busy?
What did they see near Rasht?
Why did Sara like the rain?
options: the air was cooler and the earth smelt fresh

questions.q: What did they eat in the restaurant?
What happened on the way back to Tehran?

after: For Tehranis, شمال 'the north' means the Caspian provinces of Gilan, Mazandaran and Golestan: green forests, tea gardens, rice fields and a lot of rain, only a few hours from the dry capital. Friday is Iran's weekly day off and many people are free on Thursday too, so on a Thursday morning the roads north are full. Kateh (کته) is everyday rice in the north – cooked until the water is absorbed, without draining – and ماهی سفید, the Caspian white fish, is also eaten at Nowruz. Notice the comparatives: سبزتر 'greener', خنک‌تر 'cooler', از استخر بزرگ‌تر 'bigger than the pool', and از هر غذایی خوشمزه‌تر 'tastier than any food' – the Persian way to say 'the tastiest of all'. خوابش برد 'she fell asleep' is literally 'her sleep took (her) away'; ending -ash changes with the person: خوابم برد 'I fell asleep'.
